 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226
And 227 Of The Constitution Of India, Praying To
Declare That Sub-Sections 1 & 5 Of Sections 3-G, 3-J
And Sub-Section-5 Of Section 3-H Of The National
Highways Act, 1956 As Amended By Act 16 Of 1997 As
Unconstitutional And Strike Down The Same And Etc.,

This Petition Coming On For Final Hearing This
Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The subject matter of this Writ Petition is substantially similar to the one in W.P.No.38104/2013 between M/S INDUS TECH PARK PVT LTD., and THE SLAO & ANOTHER, disposed off by this Court on 13.03.2023 whereby some reprieve has been granted to the litigant therein.

Operative portion of the judgment reads as under:
"In view of the above, the Writ Petition is allowed in terms of prayer No.3 and the Respondents are directed to compute the solatium part of the compensation reckoned from the date of taking actual possession of the subject land and pay it to the Petitioner with statutory rate of interest, within a period of three months, if he establishes his credentials in accordance with law."
2. All the contentions that had been urged in that case are repeated by the learned panel Counsel appearing for the Respondents in this case also and the same having been rejected there, Court cannot take a U-turn here, absolutely there being no justification whatsoever therefor.

A Constitutional Court cannot act as if it is playing a game of dice with abundance of unpredictability Payanat Kodaserry vs The Union Of India on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154576663/
2 of result.

sentences.text: Once a relief is granted to a litigant in a given circumstance, the same cannot be denied to others filling the very same circumstance.

An argument to the contrary cannot be sustained without bruising the principle of equality constitutionally enacted in Article 14.
3.

There is force in the submission of learned counsel for the Petitioner that the award to the extent not covering the solatium and its statutory accompaniments has to be reframed to that extent, the one having attained finality by virtue of statutory arbitration at the hands of the jurisdictional Deputy Commissioner.

This having been said, learned Panel Counsel appearing for the NHAI is also equally justified in contending that the arbitral award secured at the hands of the Deputy Commissioner cannot be examined by the Writ Court when it is open to the land owner to lay a challenge thereto u/s 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as has been held by this Court in a catena of decisions.

In view of the above, this Writ Petition is allowed in part; the competent authority shall award to the land owner the solatium & its statutory accompaniments such as interest to be reckoned from the date the possession of subject land was taken over, within a period of three months, failing which,
delay of each day shall carry addl. interest at the rate of 2% per mensem payable personally by the erring official.

It is open to the Petitioner to lay a challenge to the arbitral award u/s 34 of the 1996 Act within a period of eight weeks and if appropriate proceedings are accordingly instituted, they shall not be dismissed as being time barred.
All contentions of the parties are kept open.
This concession is shown keeping in view the principles enacted in section 14 of the Limitation Act, 1963 in view of the long pendency of Writ Petition, for no fault of the land loser.
No costs.
